source.original_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let S be its literal unit-norm subtype. The actual angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)) is jointly continuous and measurable on S×S. For every pair it lies between zero and pi, equals Mathlib's unoriented vector angle, dominates the ambient chord norm, vanishes exactly on the diagonal, and is symmetric. It satisfies the triangle inequality. These are explicit properties of the angular cost; no inherited chord-distance instance is replaced, no path-length geodesic-distance identification or Wasserstein theorem is included, and no sphere nonemptiness or positive dimension is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem result
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
      (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
        c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧
        ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
        (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
      ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w)

blind_reconstruction.text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure, define S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1}, with the inherited topology and measurable structure. Write u_bar for the ambient representative of u in S. Define the actual real function c:S times S->R by c(u,v)=Real.arccos(inner_product_E(u_bar,v_bar)), using the principal real inverse cosine. Then c is jointly continuous for the product of the inherited topologies and is measurable for the product measurable structure. For every u,v in S, all six pairwise conclusions hold: 0<=c(u,v); c(u,v)<=pi; c(u,v)=InnerProductGeometry.angle(u_bar,v_bar); norm_E(u_bar-v_bar)<=c(u,v); c(u,v)=0 if and only if u=v as subtype points; and c(u,v)=c(v,u). For every u,v,w in S the triangle inequality c(u,w)<=c(u,v)+c(v,w) holds. In the angle formula, angle(a,b)=arccos(inner_product(a,b)/(norm(a)*norm(b))); because these representatives have norm exactly 1, that denominator is exactly 1. Thus no zero-denominator convention is needed when identifying the two displayed formulas on S, despite real division being totalized in general. Equality of subtype points is equality of their ambient representatives. The continuity, measurability, range, angle identity, chord comparison, zero characterization, symmetry and triangle inequality are all conclusions; no such property of c is assumed. No positive dimension or nonempty sphere is required. If E has dimension zero, S is empty, so pair and triple universal assertions are vacuous and the empty-domain function still has the asserted continuity and measurability. The theorem concerns this specific real function on the inherited structures. It does not install or quantify a new MetricSpace distance, identify c with a geodesic or path-length distance, assert path existence, or assert a Wasserstein or transport API result.

import Mathlib.Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.TriangleInequality
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Bounds
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

open scoped InnerProductSpace
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost

private theorem chord_le_angle
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) :
    ‖u-v‖ ≤ InnerProductGeometry.angle u v := by
  let θ := InnerProductGeometry.angle u v
  have hθ : 0 ≤ θ := InnerProductGeometry.angle_nonneg u v
  have hc : Real.cos θ = ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ := by
    simpa [θ,hu,hv] using InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle u v
  have heq : ‖u-v‖^2 = 2-2*Real.cos θ := by
    rw [norm_sub_sq_real,hu,hv,hc]
    ring
  have hh := Real.sin_sq_eq_half_sub (θ/2)
  have htwo : 2*(θ/2) = θ := by ring
  rw [htwo] at hh
  have hs := Real.sin_sq_le_sq (x := θ/2)
  change ‖u-v‖ ≤ θ
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (u-v)]

theorem unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
      (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
        c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧
        ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
        (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
      ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w) := by
  dsimp only
  letI : SecondCountableTopology E := inferInstance
  have heq (u v : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}) :
      Real.arccos ⟪u.1,v.1⟫_ℝ = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 := by
    simp [InnerProductGeometry.angle,u.property,v.property]
  have hc : Continuous (fun z : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1} × {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1} =>
      Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ) := by fun_prop
  refine ⟨hc,hc.measurable,?_,?_⟩
  · intro u v
    have hchord : ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ Real.arccos ⟪u.1,v.1⟫_ℝ := by
      rw [heq]
      exact chord_le_angle u.1 v.1 u.property v.property
    refine ⟨Real.arccos_nonneg _,Real.arccos_le_pi _,heq u v,hchord,?_,?_⟩
    · constructor
      · intro hz
        apply Subtype.ext
        apply sub_eq_zero.mp
        apply norm_eq_zero.mp
        exact le_antisymm (by simpa only [hz] using hchord) (norm_nonneg _)
      · rintro rfl
        rw [heq]
        apply InnerProductGeometry.angle_self
        intro hz
        have hh := u.property
        rw [hz,norm_zero] at hh
        norm_num at hh
    · rw [heq,heq,InnerProductGeometry.angle_comm]
  · intro u v w
    rw [heq,heq,heq]
    exact InnerProductGeometry.angle_le_angle_add_angle u.1 v.1 w.1

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost

steps.title: Identify the angle
steps.text: Unit norms cancel the denominator in the vector-angle definition, so the literal arccos cost is the existing unoriented angle. Continuity follows from continuous subtype coercions, the inner product and arccos; finite dimension supplies second countability for the measurable product.

steps.text: Set θ=c(u,v)=angle(u,v). For unit endpoints, expand the squared chord norm. The half-angle identity and sin squared bounded by its argument squared yield the chord estimate; both norms and the angle are nonnegative.
